question: What is a Generative Model in Artificial Intelligence, and how does it learn patterns from existing data to generate new content such as text, images, audio, video, or synthetic data?
options: A model that maps training inputs to categories but does not learn to create new examples.
A system that retrieves matching training files whenever someone requests new text, images, or audio.
A model that learns data patterns and generates fresh examples by sampling those learned patterns.
A model that improves existing images by labeling each object and preserving the original pixels.
short: In simple words: A generative model learns patterns from examples, then uses those patterns to make new text, pictures, sounds, or other data.
technical: Correct: C. Generative models aim to represent important patterns in the examples they see, then use those patterns to produce additional samples. For instance, text generators can predict and sample words, while image generators can synthesize pixels or latent image features. Some models are conditional on prompts; others sample unconditionally. Generating does not require retrieving a stored training file, although models can sometimes memorize training content.

question: What is Tokenization in Natural Language Processing (NLP), and why must text be divided into smaller units called tokens before it can be processed by language models?
options: It rewrites every sentence into simpler English before a language model begins processing the message.
It divides text into smaller units that a language model can turn into numeric inputs.
It removes rare words from sentences so the model only reads common vocabulary items.
It labels each sentence as positive or negative before any neural network performs calculations.
short: In simple words: Tokenization cuts text into manageable pieces. The model turns those pieces into numbers so it can process the message.
technical: Correct: B. Tokenization breaks raw text into smaller units called tokens. An LLM cannot directly run attention over raw text characters. Its tokenizer uses a defined vocabulary to map tokens to numeric IDs, which the model uses to look up vectors. Tokens can be whole words, subwords, characters, or byte-derived pieces depending on the tokenizer.

question: What is an Embedding Vector in Deep Learning, and how can a word, image, or other piece of information be represented as a list of numbers that a Neural Network can process?
options: It gives each item one fixed identifier that serves as its complete meaning.
It maps an item to learned numbers that describe useful patterns and relationships.
It turns each item into frequency counts without learning any semantic relationships.
It stores an exact compressed copy of each item for direct reconstruction later.
short: In simple words: An embedding vector is a list of learned numbers that describes an item. A network uses those numbers to process or compare the item.
technical: Detailed explanation: Embedding vectors represent data items as learned feature coordinates. Different encoders can embed text, images, and other modalities, but outputs from distinct models are not automatically comparable unless aligned. Coordinates normally describe distributed patterns rather than clean human labels, and embeddings are not necessarily lossless copies of the inputs.

question: What is a Vector Database in Artificial Intelligence, and how does it store and search numerical representations of information such as text, images, and documents instead of relying only on traditional keyword-based searches?
options: It keeps documents only as keyword lists, then requires the searcher to match exact words.
It stores embeddings and searches nearby vectors, often linking results to their original documents.
It replaces every document with a summary and uses no numerical comparison during search.
It stores image pixels as database columns, then searches documents using fixed alphabetical ordering.
short: In simple words: A vector database stores number patterns that represent information. It looks for similar patterns, helping you find related documents even without matching words.
technical: Correct: B. An embedding model converts document or image content into vectors. A vector database stores and indexes the vectors, IDs, and often text or metadata, so it can rank nearby vectors using similarity rather than only exact keywords.

question: What is an AI Agent Framework, and how does it help developers build AI agents that can understand instructions, make decisions, use tools, and complete tasks beyond simply generating text responses?
options: An agent framework trains language models from scratch before they can answer customer questions.
A reusable toolkit connecting models, tools, and workflows so agents can decide and perform tasks.
A chat interface that improves writing style but cannot interact with external business software or data.
A monitoring dashboard that tracks tool errors but does not coordinate an agent's decisions.
short: In simple words: An agent framework helps AI choose safe tools, use their results, and finish tasks instead of stopping after a written reply.
technical: Correct: B. Frameworks provide agent runtimes that connect LLM decisions to tool schemas, execution policies, stored state, memory, and multi-step control flow. A chatbot may simply answer in words; a framework can coordinate tool usage to satisfy a task. The model proposes actions, but the application must authorize tools, validate arguments, observe results, and enforce stopping conditions. An agent framework is not a guarantee of autonomy, safety, or accuracy.

question: What is Supervised Learning in Machine Learning, and how does a computer learn to make predictions by studying examples that contain both input data and correct answers (labels)?
options: It groups unlabeled samples by similarity and discovers possible categories without correct answers.
It learns from labeled examples, then predicts an answer for unseen input data.
It copies labeled examples into memory and only recognizes completely identical future records.
It follows human-written rules for every input instead of learning from labeled examples.
short: In simple words: Supervised learning is like practicing with an answer key. A model sees examples with correct answers, then learns to predict answers for new examples.
technical: Detailed explanation: Supervised training examples each contain features X and a known target y. For example, an email's words are inputs while spam or inbox is its label. The model learns a relationship from X to y, then predicts outcomes for new inputs whose correct labels are unknown. To measure generalization, evaluate using held-out examples rather than the training set.

question: What is Reinforcement Learning in Artificial Intelligence, and how does an AI agent learn to make better decisions through trial and error by interacting with an environment and receiving rewards or penalties?
options: The agent memorizes labeled examples, then chooses actions without interacting with any environment.
The agent follows a fixed hand-coded path and receives rewards only after deployment.
The agent tries actions, observes consequences, and improves choices using reward feedback.
The agent estimates one correct action from each input without testing its consequences.
short: In simple words: An agent tries decisions, sees what happens, and uses rewards as feedback. After many attempts, it learns which actions work better.
technical: Detailed explanation: Reinforcement learning trains a policy through interactions with an environment. At each step, the agent receives an observation or state, chooses an action, and obtains a reward and a next observation. Training aims to improve expected cumulative return, not necessarily each immediate reward. Feedback may be positive, negative, sparse, or delayed. Examples include simulated game-playing, robotic control, or resource management.

question: What is Computer Vision in Artificial Intelligence, and how does it enable computers to understand and interpret visual information from images and videos, such as recognizing objects, identifying faces, and understanding scenes?
options: It stores image files in folders and uses filenames to guess what appears inside.
It analyzes pixels in images and videos to identify objects, faces, and scene information.
It converts every picture into written instructions before any visual pattern can be detected.
It improves camera resolution automatically by adding missing pixels and fixing lighting conditions.
short: In simple words: Computer vision helps computers recognize what appears in pictures and videos. It can spot objects, people, or parts of a scene.
technical: Correct: B. Models learn visual features from pixels and use those features to classify scenes, recognize suitable object or face categories, and locate relevant content. Their results are predictions that need accuracy and robustness checks.

question: What is Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Artificial Intelligence, and how does it enable computers to read, understand, interpret, and generate human language such as English, Telugu, and other languages?
options: An AI method that turns human language into rules which computers can only store as text.
NLP lets computers understand human language and generate useful text or speech in different languages.
A system that converts every sentence into English before a computer can correctly recognize its meaning.
A technology that only converts spoken audio into words, without analyzing or generating written language.
short: In simple words: NLP helps computers work with human language. It can understand a Telugu or English message and produce a useful reply.
technical: Correct: B. NLP is the branch of AI that processes human language in written or spoken form. Applications include classification, extraction, translation, summarization, and generation. Models transform words or subwords into numerical features, learn patterns in context, and produce task-specific outputs. English, Telugu, and other languages may be supported depending on training data. NLP does not require converting everything into English first.

question: What is a Diffusion Model in Generative Artificial Intelligence, and how can it create realistic images, audio, or other data by starting with random noise and gradually transforming it into meaningful content?
options: It memorizes sample images and combines their pixels directly when creating new pictures later.
It creates images by decoding a fixed code without using any learned noise removal process.
It starts with noise and repeatedly removes it, gradually forming a new realistic sample.
It creates each image in one pass by choosing the closest picture from training.
short: In simple words: Diffusion models are like repeatedly cleaning a blurry picture. They learn tiny improvements until random noise becomes a believable new image or sound.
technical: Detailed explanation: A diffusion generative model learns how to reverse a staged noise-corruption process. In common DDPM training, real data is corrupted at randomly selected noise levels, and a neural network learns to estimate the noise. Generation typically begins with Gaussian noise and repeatedly uses the learned denoiser to produce a new sample. Variants have been used for images, audio, video and other structured data; realism is not guaranteed on every run.
